name: Direct Volume Rendering with Precomputed Occlusion (DOS)
definition: A volume rendering technique that performs ray marching in a single pass per slice, using precomputed 2D occlusion maps to approximate the attenuation of light from rays behind the current sample, avoiding the need for full volumetric integration or multiple passes for occlusion.
summary: Direct Volume Rendering with Precomputed Occlusion is a single-pass technique that approximates volumetric attenuation using precomputed 2D occlusion maps to solve self-occlusion without full volumetric integration.
